items.title: Shape and color come first
items.simple: In heavy fog, you may see only a sign's shape. From far away, you see the color before you can read the words. Shape and color tell you the message early.
items.official: In poor visibility conditions, such as heavy fog, you may be able to make out only the shape of a sign. As you approach a sign and while still distant, you may see the color long before you can read the message or see the symbol, giving you some advance information.
items.mnemonic: Shape in the fog, color from far, words up close.

items.title: Red and white: stop or no
items.simple: Red with white means stop, yield, do not, or no. Stop signs, Yield signs, Do Not Enter signs and Wrong Way signs are all red and white.
items.official: Red used with white conveys stop, yield, do not, and no. Stop signs, yield signs, do not enter or wrong way signs, the circle and slash in a no turn sign, and the restrictions in a parking sign are examples.

items.title: Black and white: the law
items.simple: Black with white means a rule set by law. Speed limit, Do Not Pass and no-turn signs are black and white. You must obey them.
items.official: Black used with white conveys regulatory information. Speed limit, do not pass, no turns are examples where the operation is regulated by law and the black and white sign would be found. Regulatory signs inform you of the law; you must obey their instructions.
items.mnemonic: Black and white, like a rule book.

items.title: Yellow and black: warning
items.simple: Yellow with black means warning. It tells you about something ahead, like a curve, a stop ahead, a low overpass, or a slippery road.
items.official: Yellow used with black conveys a warning. Curve ahead, stop ahead, overhead clearances, slippery when wet, are all examples.

items.title: Yellow-green: people nearby
items.simple: A bright yellow-green sign is a special warning. It means a school zone, people walking, or people on bikes may be near. Watch for them.
items.official: A specialized class of warning signs uses a strong yellow/green color with black to advise of school zone, pedestrian and/or bicyclist activities.

items.title: Green: where to go
items.simple: A green and white sign gives helpful information. It tells you about places you are going, like the cities on this sign.
items.official: Green and white, blue and white, and brown and white signs are used to provide helpful information. The green sign is used to provide destination types of information.

items.title: Blue: services for drivers
items.simple: A blue and white sign tells you about services for drivers, like the gas pump and bed shown on this sign.
items.official: Green and white, blue and white, and brown and white signs are used to provide helpful information. The blue sign is used to inform regarding motorists services.
items.mnemonic: Blue is for services for you.

items.title: Brown: history and culture
items.simple: A brown and white sign tells you about a place of history or culture in the area, like a historic site.
items.official: The brown sign is used to advise of historical or cultural interests that might exist in the area.
items.mnemonic: Brown, like an old history book.

items.title: Orange: construction work zone
items.simple: Orange with black means construction. You are in a work zone. Slow down and be alert. Black and white signs there may show extra work zone rules.
items.official: Orange and black and pink and black signs are used to advise and warn in construction (orange) and incident (pink) areas. They are used with black and white signs that convey regulations that might exist only because of the construction effort or the incident.
items.mnemonic: Orange cones, orange signs: work zone.

items.title: Pink: incident area
items.simple: A pink and black sign warns you about an incident area ahead. Slow down and use care as you drive through.
items.official: Orange and black and pink and black signs are used to advise and warn in construction (orange) and incident (pink) areas.
items.mnemonic: Pink is incident. Orange is construction.

items.title: Octagon: always stop
items.simple: A sign with 8 sides always means stop. Stop all the way at the sign, stop line, crosswalk or curb. Wait until the way is clear.
items.official: Octagon (Stop): This eight-sided shape always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the sign, stop line, pedestrian crosswalk or curb. Wait for any vehicle or pedestrian to clear the way.

items.title: Triangle: yield
items.simple: A triangle sign means yield. Slow down as you come to the crossing. Be ready to stop. Let cars, people walking and bikes go first.
items.official: Triangle (Yield): You must slow down as you come to the intersection. Be prepared to stop. Let any vehicles, pedestrians or bicyclists safely pass before you proceed.

items.title: Tall rectangle: tells the law
items.simple: A tall rectangle sign usually gives you an instruction or tells you the law. Speed Limit and Do Not Pass signs are tall rectangles.
items.official: Rectangle (Regulatory or Guide): Vertical signs generally give instructions or tell you the law.

items.title: Wide rectangle: directions
items.simple: A wide rectangle sign may give you directions or information, like which way to go to a city.
items.official: Rectangle (Regulatory or Guide): Horizontal signs may give directions or information.

items.title: Diamond: warning ahead
items.simple: A diamond sign warns you of a special condition or hazard ahead. Slow down. Drive with care. Be ready to stop.
items.official: Diamond (Warning): These signs warn you of special conditions or hazards ahead. Slow down and drive with caution. Be ready to stop.

items.title: Pentagon: school zone
items.simple: A sign with 5 sides, shaped like a house, marks a school zone or a school crossing. Two signs may be used together to show where the crosswalk is.
items.official: Pentagon (School Zone/School Crossing): This five-sided shape marks school zones and warns you about school crossings. Two signs may be used together to show the actual location of the crosswalk.

items.title: Red circle and slash: NO
items.simple: A red circle with a slash means NO. Look at the picture inside the circle. That is the thing you may not do.
items.official: Regulatory signs inform you of the law; you must obey their instructions. Remember that a red circle with a slash means NO; the symbol inside the circle tells you what is prohibited.
items.mnemonic: Slash means NO. The picture shows what.

items.title: Pennant: no passing zone
items.simple: This yellow sign is shaped like a flag. It marks the start of a no passing zone. Do not pass cars ahead of you in your lane, even if the way is clear.
items.official: No Passing Zone: This sign marks the beginning of a no passing zone. You may not pass cars ahead of you in your lane, even if the way is clear.

items.title: Round RR sign: tracks ahead
items.simple: The round yellow sign with an X and two R's warns that a railroad crossing is ahead. Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop for trains.
items.official: Railroad Crossing: Advance warning signs are placed before a railroad crossing. These signs warn you to look, listen, slow down and be prepared to stop for trains or any vehicles using the rails.
items.mnemonic: Round sign, rails ahead: look and listen.

items.title: Crossbuck: railroad crossing
items.simple: The white X-shaped crossbuck marks a railroad crossing. Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Trains may come from either direction, on any track.
items.official: Railroad Crossbuck: This sign is a warning of a railroad crossing. Look, listen, slow down and be prepared to stop for trains or any vehicles using the rails. Trains may be approaching from either direction. If there is more than one track, trains may be approaching from either direction on either track.
